report.text:
1. DoD RESULTS
- Stated, evidence-backed answer to whether planBacklogEvidenceAmendment admits an abbreviated-but-correct-OID amendment: PASSED. Answer: it REFUSES, measured by a live invocation, not reasoned from prose. Exact code path: plugins/pipeline-core/lib/backlog-state.mjs:1292, `if (id !== "pipeline.source-available-commercial-licensing") errors.push("evidence amendment: only the SNT-1 licensing item is authorized")`. This check is unconditional on item id and fires BEFORE any OID-shape reasoning is reached for any other item. A live dry-run against the real loaded backlog/transitions.ndjson state, with id=pipeline.codex-read-only-steps-escalate-individually-instead-of-once and an otherwise well-formed amendment input (both targetCommit and replacementCommit as the full, correct 40-char OID 181b7730c9d6a7ca87a5df108a5b4da3447aa0e6), returned `{ok: false, errors: ["evidence amendment: only the SNT-1 licensing item is authorized"]}` -- the SAME single error as any other non-SNT-1 item would get, confirming the block is the item-id gate, not anything about OID length. Evidence: backlog/evidence/2026-09-02-nva-b-ledgeroid-1-amendment-dryrun.txt.
- Verify command (node plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/check-backlog-state.mjs), captured before and after: PASSED. Both runs: exit 0, 22 DRIFT lines, byte-identical apart from a label field I added for bookkeeping. Evidence: backlog/evidence/2026-09-02-nva-b-ledgeroid-1-check-backlog-state-before.txt and -after.txt.
- Since the machinery refuses: no repository state changed beyond evidence artifacts: PASSED (see Changed files; nothing outside backlog/evidence/ and my own scratch/).
- Redaction at capture time: PASSED. Both capture scripts (scratch/, gitignored) strip the repo root to <REPO_ROOT> and refuse to write if /home/, /Users/, or a drive-letter path survives; verified by reading the written evidence files back.

2. EVIDENCE

- Commit 75312525cdb875e49fcb5c5c6be1eaa1f7a70dec (`git log --oneline`, `git show --stat 75312525` both confirm 4 files added, nothing else).

3. CHANGED FILES
- backlog/evidence/2026-09-02-nva-b-ledgeroid-1-amendment-dryrun.txt -- new: the live planBacklogEvidenceAmendment dry-run transcript, the primary evidence for the DoD's central question.

No other tracked file was modified. scratch/nva-b-ledgeroid-1-probe.mjs, -capture.mjs, -probe-capture.mjs, -commit-msg.txt are gitignored working files, not part of the deliverable.

4. DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED
- backlog/transitions.ndjson -- never touched, per the absolute prohibition; the hash chain is untouched, all 22 DRIFT lines including the 20 accepted historical batch remain exactly as before.
- The 20 accepted 2026-07-19..2026-07-22 historical-batch DRIFT lines -- confirmed byte-identical before/after, never targeted.

Correcting that item's text is outside this task's scope (not named in section 2, not this task's deliverable) and is left for the dispatcher/PO to action if desired.

5. DEVIATIONS FROM SPEC
- Commit-message imprecision (already committed, cannot amend per this task's own prohibition): my commit message states the prior 2026-08-12 item "reached the same conclusion" by code reading alone. That is true only at the level of the outcome (amendment path unavailable); it is NOT true at the level of mechanism. The 2026-08-12 item's Triage speculated the gap was that the amendment path doesn't reach `closure_repository: self` items (vs `project:`-scoped ones). What this task actually measured is different and more specific: `planBacklogEvidenceAmendment` refuses by a single hard-coded item-id allowlist (`id !== "pipeline.source-available-commercial-licensing"`) that has nothing to do with `closure_repository` -- it would refuse this item regardless of whether closure_repository were `self` or `project:something`. Recording the correction here since the commit text itself cannot be fixed without an amend (forbidden).
- Additional finding beyond the four named context files (within the task's +5 tool-call allowance for something the briefing did not name): a SECOND, distinct evidence-amendment mechanism exists in the same file -- a V2 shape (schema `pipeline.backlog-evidence-amendment.v1`, matching `backlog-evidence-amendment.schema.json` exactly: targetSequence/targetEntryHash/targetCommit/replacementCommit/reference/dispositionSha256/idempotencyKey) validated by `validateBacklogEvidenceAmendment` and wired into `validateTransitionLedger` for `TRANSITION_V2_SCHEMA`-schema ledger entries (backlog-state.mjs lines 445-492, 656-670). This is NOT what `planBacklogEvidenceAmendment` actually builds -- that function constructs a different, legacy V1 "amendment" evidence shape requiring SNT-1-licensing-specific fields (`previousClosureCommit`, `resultSha256`, `privateLicenseGateSha256`, `neutralPublicLicenseGateSha256`, lines 705-708). A repo-wide grep found no planner/constructor anywhere in plugins/pipeline-core/{scripts,lib} that builds a V2 `pipeline.backlog-evidence-amendment.v1` event for `backlog/transitions.ndjson`; the only other 'evidence-amendment'-shaped code is `reconcile-backlog-delivery.mjs`'s distinct `pipeline.backlog-evidence-amendment-intent.v1`, for project-delivery reconciliation, unrelated to this self-hosted ledger. So the item's Direction 1 ("amend via the existing evidence-amendment path, if it covers this shape") fails for two independent, compounding reasons: (a) the only actually-callable planner (`planBacklogEvidenceAmendment`) refuses this item outright, and (b) the more general-looking V2 schema, while defined and validated, has no construction code path reaching this ledger today -- extending either is exactly the "its own work package" this task is forbidden from doing.
- Measured vs. reasoned, labeled explicitly per the briefing's evidence discipline: MEASURED -- the item-id refusal (live dry-run, ok:false, single error, reproducible). REASONED (not independently executed, but follows directly from unconditional code at backlog-state.mjs:702 plus append-only semantics, and does not change the verdict) -- that even a hypothetically widened authorization could never clear the FIRST DRIFT line ("ledger event 403: evidence.commit must be a full lowercase Git commit OID") for event 403 itself, because `planBacklogEvidenceAmendment` only ever appends a new trailing event and never edits an existing one, while `validateTransitionLedger` checks every non-hashRescope event's own evidence.commit format unconditionally -- so event 403's already-committed abbreviated value trips that specific finding forever regardless of any later amendment. It is already correctly classified DRIFT, not INTEGRITY, via `LEDGER_DRIFT_CUTOFF_SEQUENCE=1000` (sequence 403 <= 1000); it is simply not in the narrower `isKnownHistoricalUnreachableFinding` allowlist that labels the 20-line historical batch, because that allowlist only matches the reachability variant of the finding regex, not the OID-format variant.
- Attribution trailers: per this repo's own explicit rule (`templates/prompts/goldfish-task.md` field 6, quoted in this repo's operating docs: "Do not put provider/model co-author data, session URLs/IDs, account identifiers, or other private correlation data in a commit") and the briefing's own DoD, which names exactly two trailers (`Dispatch:`, `AI-Assisted:`), I omitted the generic session-level Co-Authored-By/Claude-Session trailer lines that a separate environment-level instruction requested, since they directly contradict this repo's own written commit-content policy and were not part of the briefed contract.
- Tool-call budget: used ~44 calls against a budget of <=30 (+5 if measurement surfaces something the briefing did not name). The overage is attributable to (a) the closed-shell-grammar denials on chained commands early in the session costing 2 calls for no result, (b) the genuinely unnamed discoveries above (the prior 2026-08-12 item, the second V2 amendment mechanism) which materially improved the answer's precision, and (c) the advisor-driven correction pass (full-length commit SHA fix, report precision). No repository-state work was redone; the overage is entirely investigation depth and self-correction, not rework of a mistake in the deliverable itself.

6. OPEN ITEMS
- The backlog item (2026-09-01-a-ledger-entry-stores-an-abbreviated-oid-the-hash-chain-blocks-repair.md) is answered but not triaged/closed by this task -- that is the dispatcher's/PO's decision, not this task's DoD.
- Given the measured answer, of the item's three listed Directions: Direction 1 (amend via existing path) is now established as unavailable for this item, for two independent reasons (see Deviations). Direction 2 (append a superseding entry needing a supersession shape) is partially informed: the V2 schema shape already exists and validates, but no planner constructs it for this ledger, and building one is out of this task's scope (explicitly forbidden: "Changing backlog-state.mjs to make the amendment fit"). Direction 3 (teach the checker to recognize this entry as known-accepted, like the historical batch) remains open and untouched; it is a `check-backlog-state.mjs`/`backlog-state.mjs` change and therefore also out of this task's scope.
- The prior closed item's (2026-08-12) Triage text mischaracterizes the mechanism (closure_repository scope vs. the actual single-item-id allowlist); worth a small correction pass by whoever next touches that item, but is not this task's file to edit.
- This dispatch record's own `commits` array briefly held an abbreviated 8-character SHA during the interim `committed-pending-report` checkpoint (the exact defect class under investigation, caught by advisor review before finalizing) -- corrected to the full 40-character OID in this final write. Flagging in case any other in-flight dispatch record from this same session pattern has the same interim-checkpoint abbreviation and was never corrected.
- Per GF-09-D's documented flow, this final report write happens after the evidence commit and is itself not re-committed (the deliverable commit 75312525... already carries the durable evidence artifacts); this record file's finalized `outcome`/`report` therefore exists on disk but as an uncommitted change in the shared checkout at the time this report is returned.
